title: Cervical biopsy
what: The doctor takes a tiny piece of tissue from the cervix. It is studied under a microscope.
why: When a smear or colposcopy shows changes and the doctor needs to know what they are.
duration: the procedure usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
Any discharge or inflammation right now

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: It is usually done in the first days after your period ends. Not during your period.

prepare.title: 2 days before
prepare.text: No sex, tampons, douching, or vaginal suppositories, unless your doctor says otherwise.

prepare.title: Painkiller
prepare.text: You can ask your doctor whether to take a painkiller beforehand.

steps: You sit in the gynecological chair
The doctor inserts a speculum and looks at the cervix through a colposcope, a magnifying device
A solution is applied to the cervix to show the changed area
A tiny piece of tissue is taken with special forceps
If it bleeds, the spot is treated
feel: Period-like cramping for a few minutes
Sometimes mild dizziness. Tell the doctor
after: Light bloody or dark discharge, usually for a few days
No sex, tampons, baths, or pools, usually for 1 to 2 weeks. Your doctor will say exactly
Your doctor will explain the result at your visit
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), severe pain, or bad-smelling discharge

faq.q: If they are doing a biopsy, does it mean cancer?
faq.a: No. Most often the changes are benign. A biopsy is needed to know for sure.
Usually like a brief pinch and cramp. It does not last long.

reminders.text: Cervical biopsy tomorrow. No sex or tampons today. Bring your smear results and a pad.
